title: Widen the model: dim 512 -> 640 at depth 12
description: ASPECT_RATIO 40 -> 48, so model_dim goes 512 -> 640 with 5 heads of 128; depth 12 and everything else unchanged.
reflection: FLAT/slightly negative: val_bpb 0.986702 vs baseline 0.986277 (+0.0004, inside the ~0.0009 noise floor). Numbers: params 71.3M -> 100.9M, FLOPs/token 3.46e8 -> 5.03e8 (+45%), total_tokens 331M -> 246M (-26%), num_steps 1878, steady-state MFU 38.5% -> 41.5%, peak VRAM 32.1 -> 40.7 GB. Reading: at this compute budget we are now AT the compute-optimal model size, not below it -- a +41% parameter increase bought exactly enough quality per token to pay for the 26% token loss and no more. That is the same 1:1 trade the batch axis showed in round 0, and it is the natural end of the capacity climb that depth 8->10 (-0.0082) and 10->12 (-0.0027) traced out. Width is not a cheaper direction than depth; both are now flat. Also worth recording: VRAM 40.7GB, and MFU rose to 41.5%, so throughput is no longer the limiter either. The remaining runs should go to structure that changes quality per FLOP at roughly fixed size -- MLP expansion ratio, window pattern, or the one untouched schedule constant (WARMDOWN_RATIO) -- not to more parameters.
